sources.title: PlayStation Cancels Live-Service Heist Shooter, Fairgames
sources.text: Fairgames , a live-service heist game from PlayStation's Haven Studios, has been canceled by Sony. A new report from Bloomberg reveals that Fairgames has been scrapped, three and a half years after its announcement. Developer Haven Studios will not be shut down, nor will there be any layoffs, as PlayStation has decided to turn the team into a support studio for other first-party projects. The decision to pull the plug on the game was made after a recent test did not meet internal expectations. “While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” said executives Sean Decker and John Doyle in a note reviewed by Bloomberg. “Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.” The test being referenced here is likely one that made some waves earlier this fall. A mysterious game known as Project Espresso, which looked a lot like Fairgames, began advertising private playtests with a gameplay trailer back in September . Not much is known about those tests, but they didn't seem to be very fruitful for the team. Fairgames was announced in 2023 and has been the subject of scrutiny for some time. Some fans pushed back on PlayStation's live-service pivot during the early 2020s, as the company has always excelled with blockbuster single-player games. When Concord bombed , fans began to express even further revulsion toward titles like Fairgames. The project has also been soured by a number of setbacks, including departures of key developers and internal struggles . Fairgames' cancelation marks yet another major failure for PlayStation's live-service efforts. Concord flopped, The Last of Us Online was scrapped , an online God of War game was killed , and Marathon has been struggling since launch. Helldivers 2, on the other hand, has been a big win for PlayStation. There's some hope that maybe Bungie's decision to revive Destiny 2 could be productive , but Sony seems to be moving away from live-service. The only other major live-service game from PlayStation on the horizon is 4:Loop , a new game from JJ Abrams' studio, Bad Robot. We'll see if it suffers a similar fate as these other titles. Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

sources.text: Haven Games to "shift focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation" PlayStation has cancelled Fairgames, the live-service shooter previously in development at its Montreal-based subsidiary Haven Studios. In a statement to Bloomberg , PlayStation said Haven Studios will "shift focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." No jobs have been cut due to the cancellation. According to an email reviewed by Bloomberg, executives Sean Decker and John Doyle informed employees that a recent Fairgames playtest did not meet expectations. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," they said. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." Haven Studios' debut game was announced in 2023, initially scheduled for release last year, and later delayed to Spring 2026. Jade Raymond founded Haven Studios in 2021, and PlayStation Studios acquired the studio in 2022. Following Raymond's departure in May 2025 , executive producer Marie-Eve Danis and Pierre-François Sapinski were appointed co-studio heads. PlayStation started focusing on the live-service market in 2022 by acquiring Bungie for $3.6 billion . Former Sony Interactive Entertainment head Jim Ryan said the company aimed to launch more than ten live-service games by 2026 . Sony reduced the value of its acquisition by $765 million in the 2025/26 fiscal year after Destiny 2 and Marathon underperformed. Earlier this year, Bungie laid off 292 employees and ended development on Destiny 2. Following the game's final update, Bungie announced plans to reinstate vaulted campaigns , raids, and destinations to restore player trust. One of Sony’s most publicised live-service failures was Concord in 2024 , which was withdrawn from sale two weeks after release. Sony subsequently closed its developer Firewalk Studios , along with Neon Koi. Koi. In 2025, Sony cancelled two unannounced live service titles from Bend Studio and Bluepoint Games. The following year, Sony closed Bluepoint, resulting in 70 job losses . Sony Interactive CEO Hideaki Nishino previously said he wanted to "revitalise" live-service projects through a combination of first- and third-party content following its string of failures. "We believe that live service games are content that attracts users on a global level, so we want to continue to revitalise the market through both first-party and third-party content," Nishino said. "We are not only focusing on promoting new releases, but also considering what we can do with older titles in the medium to long term." He continued: "With live service games, it's important to continuously provide something. The genre itself is relatively new, and I think many people are trying various things, so we also want to continue to take on challenges within that context."

sources.text: After a long development, it’s being reported that Fairgames is no more PlayStation has reportedly cancelled its upcoming live service game, Fairgames. As reported by Bloomberg , PlayStation says it cancelled Fairgames after the results of a recent playtest “fell short of the goals we had set.” It comes three years after Fairgames was initially revealed in 2023. “While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” reads a note reportedly penned by executives Sean Decker and John Doyle. âCombined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.” Footage from this playtest seemingly leaked online in September . If this was indeed Fairgames, then it was the first piece of gameplay footage we had seen. Other than that, all we had to go on were cinematics in the announcement trailer from 2023. It is being reported that developer Haven Studios will not be closing down as a result of this decision, nor will there be any layoffs. This also comes as Sony ‘s live service ventures have produced mixed results. While Helldivers 2 was a win, Concord flopped, and PlayStation went on to shut down developer Firewalk Studios. Meanwhile, Bungie is trying to grow Marathon ‘s playerbase, so it makes sense that PlayStation doesn’t want to add another live service into the mix right now. With these factors in mind, this report regarding Fairgames is unsurprising. We already knew that development was struggling behind the scenes, as it had been reported that internal playtests were negatively received as far back as 2025. If recent playtests failed to inspire either, it’s likely Sony decided not to fund the project further, especially given the state of the live service market. PlayStation is yet to publicly comment on claims that Fairgames has been cancelled.

sources.text: Sony's latest game cancellation adds to a long list of failed GaaS projects Sony has canceled Fairgames (aka Fairgame$ ) three years after the live-service shooter was announced, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday. No one at its developer, Haven Studios, is getting laid off, and instead Haven will support other Sony Interactive Entertainment-owned studios, according to that report. Farigames recently held a playtest and, according to an internal email reviewed by Bloomberg, feedback from that playtest didn't live up to PlayStation's expectations. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle said in the email. With "challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre," Sony decided to cancel the game. Fairgames reportedly had been reworked multiple times since its 2023 reveal. It would have been the debut game from Haven, which was founded in 2021 by former Assassin's Creed producer and Google Stadia Games and Entertainment head Jade Raymond , who has since left the studio. Haven was acquired by Sony in 2022 . Back in 2022, Sony announced a huge push for live-service games , aiming to release at least 10 by 2026. While games like Helldivers 2 and Gran Turismo 7 have been steady live-service hits, Sony's push has largely failed. Concord is the most notable misfire , as it was actually released before Sony reversed course and shut it down shortly after launch in embarrassing fashion. A live-service God of War game , a multiplayer The Last of Us game , and many others were canceled before they could see the light of day. PlayStation studios working on live-service games, including London Studios, Firewalk Studios, and Bluepoint Games, were all shut down in recent years. In June, Sony laid off most of the Destiny team at Bungie, as " Destiny 2 fell short of expectations" with players. Recently, Horizon Hunters Gathering was reportedly delayed so it can be rebooted in response to negative player feedback (which sounds not too dissimilar to the Fairgames situation).

sources.text: Fairgames was revealed in 2023, but nothing more was ever seen of it. A Bloomberg report says Fairgames, a PvP heist shooter announced by Haven Studios and Sony in 2023 , has been cancelled. In something of a surprising twist, a PlayStation rep told the site there will be no layoffs as a result of the cancellation, as Haven will "shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." While it was announced three years ago, work on Fairgames appears to have started even further back, in 2021. Just a couple months after her high-profile split with Google Stadia , Assassin's Creed co-creator Jade Raymond announced the formation of Haven Studios , which was "working on an unannounced new IP for PlayStation." In 2022, right around the time former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan was talking about launching 12 live service games by 2025, Sony acquired the studio outright; a year after that, Fairplay was revealed to the world. But things have not gone smoothly since then. Helldivers 2 was a massive hit, but seven of those planned games were cancelled before release . Of the remaining games, one was Marathon , which endures but has not lived up to expectations, and another was Concord , one of the most famously disastrous game launches in years, which was taken offline less than two weeks after it launched, never to return. A live-service spinoff of the Horizon series, Hunters Gathering, was also reportedly rebooted after negative feedback from playtests . A partial accounting of canned multiplayer projects: The Concord catastrophe in particular seemed to shake Sony, which began reversing its live service strategy just a few months later. Fairgames itself looked to be in trouble in 2025 when Raymond departed Haven , reportedly after an external playtest left PlayStation leadership "concerned about how the game was received and its progress." The Bloomberg report says a more recent large-scale playtest produced similar results. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email sent to Haven Studios employees. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." The one bright spot to the cancellation is that no jobs will be cut because of it: A Sony rep told Bloomberg that Haven "will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities." sources.title: PlayStation adds live-service shooter Fairgames to its constantly expanding graveyard
sources.text: Sony's trail of bodies is only getting longer Sony has dug up another plot in its expanding live-service graveyard, and is lowering the still-warm corpse of Haven Studios' Fairgames into the dirt. The shooter, which was revealed in 2023, has been canceled, though PlayStation says there will be no layoffs as a result of its decision to end the project. "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities," a PlayStation representative tells Bloomberg , who first reported the news. Fairgames was revealed in a 2023 trailer which stylized the title as "Fairgame$." The trailer featured no in-game footage, but presented a stylish version of a Payday-style shooter focused on heists. But the game never materialized again. The last major news on the project came in 2025, when Haven Studios founder Jade Raymond – a veteran Ubisoft producer who'd worked on Assassins' Creed – left the company . Bloomberg reports that Fairgames was ultimately canceled after a poor showing during a recent test session with thousands of players. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," according to an internal memo. PlayStation had apparently reworked the game multiple times since it was first revealed, and prior to the test had planned to showcase it again under a new title, according to the report. While PlayStation once had extensive plans for live-service games, it's canceled so many of those projects that it's now difficult to keep track of them all. The death of Concord just two weeks after launch is perhaps the highest profile example, but that's just the most memorable corpse among an extensive trail of bodies. A multiplayer God of War title from Bluepoint and a live-service game from Bend Studio were canceled in 2025 . A multitude of unannounced projects were iced amid mass layoffs at PlayStation in 2024, including a Twisted Metal game and an original project from the publisher's now-defunct London studio. Naughty Dog 's The Last of Us multiplayer game died in 2023 . Bungie has reportedly had numerous projects scrapped since it was acquired by Sony. PlayStation has even killed not just one , but two projects helmed by Call of Duty veteran Jason Blundell. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Sony's biggest live-service hit in recent years is certainly Helldivers 2, but it's struggled to replicate that success – heck, it's struggled to release other online games at any scale. The publisher's annual MLB The Show series remains a staple among baseball fans, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls seems to have found a niche among fighting game aficionados, and Marathon is continuing to survive, but these aren't the Fortnite-level hits Sony is clearly gunning for. I guess we'll never know whether Fairgames could've been a hit. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator. sources.title: PlayStation's embattled shooter Fairgames has finally been cancelled, a new report says, as live service push withers away
sources.text: After years of silence, we finally know the fate of PlayStation's embattled live service game Fairgames. The Haven-developed co-op heist shooter has been cancelled, with the silver lining that the studio is not closing down or laying off staff. According to a new Bloomberg report, the decision to cancel Fairgames was made following the results of a recent playtest. Sony told staff on Tuesday of the playtest's poor reception and of its decision to end development. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle reportedly wrote in an email to staff. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PvP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." A PlayStation spokesperson later confirmed that developers at Haven will now support other teams within the PlayStation Studios group, as they continue to "explore new creative opportunities". Fairgames was initially announced in 2023 as one of several in-development live service games, as part of an initiative by former PlayStation boss Jim Ryan to create more than a dozen games that generate recurring revenue . Most of those titles were cancelled before they were even revealed, and those that made it out, such as Concord, flopped severely . Even Sony darling Guerrilla Games seemingly can't make it work, with recent reports saying the studio's Horizon Hunters Gathering - initially envisioned as a live service spin on the robo dinosaur series - will now shift into a more traditional co-op structure without live service elements. That's assuming the team can show a revamped version of the game to executives by December. The news of Fairgames' cancellation isn't surprising. The game has had a tumultuous development journey ever since its reveal. Initially set for release in 2025, the game was soon pushed back to 2026 , following the departure of studio founder Jade Raymond . Though Sony later reiterated its commitment to its remaining in-development live service titles , Fairgames was never shown to the public again. That same year, game director Daniel Drapeau left Haven - another key departure suggesting the game had difficulties and might not see release. Throughout that time, Fairgames has reportedly been reworked multiple times, with a plan for it to be re-revealed under a new name. That name is believed to be Break In, linked to a trademark Sony filed in May , but with the project cancelled, we may never know if that was the case.

sources.text: Nintendo Switch 2 The Legend of Zelda The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Well, you’ve made it. You’re finally at the most infamous dungeon in all of Zelda -dom, the Water Temple of Ocarina of Time . Good news for you: In the remake, this dungeon is far, far easier than it’s ever been. A few of the edges have been sanded down, the rooms all look far more distinct and memorable so it’s less of a mental maze, and the iron boots can be equipped and de-equipped simply by pressing down on the gamepad. Compared to the original, it’s a smooth ride. But still, this is one of the most involved dungeons in the game, so buckle on that Zora Tunic and let’s get swimming. To enter the Water Temple, you need to be wearing (no, I wasn’t joking) the Zora Tunic, which you get by freeing King Zora from his ice block back in Zora Domain. To do that, you need Blue Fire in a bottle, which you obtain in the Ice Cavern as an adult. You’ll also need the Iron Boots from that same cavern. If you haven’t gotten that far yet, back yourself up and come back to this guide later. Once you’re in the temple, remove your iron boots and float to the top. Run forward, and you’ll be in a big, open room with a bunch of doors on all four sides across four different floors, and water below you. I’m going to be referring to this as the “main hall” going forward. We’re going to be here a lot. I’ll also be referring to doors by floor and cardinal direction, so if you’re ever confused about what I’m talking about, open that map. The first thing you’re going to do is slay that Blue Tektite in front of you. Sword, hookshot, whatever you like, just get it out of the way. Next, you’re going to equip those Iron Boots, descend to the first floor, and head through the east door. Once you’re inside, remove the boots to float upward for a cutscene with your fiancee, Ruto. When it’s over, grab the Dungeon Map from the chest in front of you, and then stand on the platform with the Triforce symbol and play Zelda’s Lullaby to lower the water level. Real quick tip: There are three different spots to mess with the water level in this dungeon, and each one will raise it to a different spot. This one brings it down to the first floor, and is marked by glowy blue pillars. It might be good to make a note somewhere of which color results in which water level, just in case you ever get turned around or confused and the water level is in the wrong place. Once the water has dropped, fearlessly jump down the hole, landing in the water below so it doesn’t damage you. Now, with the water taken care of, note that one of the torches in here is lit. Stand behind it with your bow equipped and aim an arrow through the fire to each of the two torches on the other end of the room to open the door in front of you, then enter. Defeat the three Spikes by blocking their attacks with your shield and swinging your sword when they’re vulnerable to obtain a Small Key. (Din’s Fire is also usable for this puzzle). Backtrack the way you came in and head out into the main hall. There are two more aptly named Spikes out here waiting for you; get rid of them. To your left (west side, 1F) is a bombable/breakable wall. Knock that out, and use your Iron Boots to sink, sink, sink. Head down the underwater corridor and take care of the Shell Blade by hitting it with your hookshot when its mouth is all the way open. At the end of the corridor, take off the boots and rise up. In here, climb the platform jutting out of the water and use the hookshot to grapple onto the pillars ahead of you. Take down the Tektites and the Like Like (Hookshot is great here), and you’ll be rewarded with the Compass. Now, all the way back to the main hall! To the west (1F) is a block you can push forward until it drops in the water. Do that, then use the boots to sink again. Look out for the Shell Blade in the way, then rise back up at the end of the hall. You’ll find yourself in a room with a whirlpool and some statues underwater, and a chest on the other side. This looks trickier than it is. Use the iron boots to drop into the whirlpool, aiming for the center platform (the serpent’s body) stretched down the middle of the pool. Stand on the platform and use your hookshot to smack the weird gem thing in the serpent’s mouth. This will unlock the underwater grate, allowing you to enter. You might need to don and doff the iron boots a few times to swim over properly, but with some careful aiming it’s very doable. There are two more Shell Blades to fight inside, after which you’re free to take off the boots, rise to the surface, and grab the small key. Back across the whirlpool, out the door, into the main hall again. There’s a locked door on the central pillar here, directly in front of you, and you now have a key. Head inside. Once inside, step forward, turn around, and look up for a grapple point. Use your hookshot to get on the platform above. Right in front of you is a spot to stand and play Zelda’s Lullaby to raise the water back up. ( Note : the columns here are green, green brings the water to 2F! Write it down if you need to!) Before you leave this inside pillar, though, jump in the water and look down: a new gap has opened up with the water level rising. Use iron boots to drop down, where three Spikes are waiting for you. Kill them with the hookshot, then use the hookshot to hit the green switch above your head, releasing a Shell Blade. Kill that too, then remove the iron boots where it was standing to rise up into the now-open area. There’s a red rupee in a chest on the way up, as well as a gold skulltula on the wall opposite. sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake removed Mario and Skyward Sword references to not "interrupt" players
sources.text: Thankfully, Skyward Sword's director says "no hard feelings" The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is, by most standards, a pretty faithful remake to the original game, but Nintendo wasn't scared to make changes where necessary. I was a little bummed to learn the fun references to the Super Mario Bros. series had been removed, not to mention some Zelda: Skyward Sword art that was in the Ocarina of Time 3DS remake, but with how carefully Nintendo positions every game, remaster, and remake into its existing portfolio, I'm not at all surprised. In case you aren't a Zelda historian, the original game has several Mario references including character portraits and heavy design influences on characters like Talon, Malon, and Ingo, who strongly resemble Mario, Peach, and Luigi, respectively. It makes a lot of sense as Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Super Mario 64 were both being made at the same time, but 30 years later, the remake doesn't share that same connection to Mario 64. That's why the portraits have been removed from the remake, even though it's still pretty clear Talon, Malon, and Ingo have doppelgangers hanging out in the Mario universe. "Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal. Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing," Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma tells Game Informer . "But looking at it now, like if a player is coming through that area, and given the overall way that we're, you know, creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, 'Why is Yoshi there?' We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time." Similarly to the original Ocarina of Time and Mario 64, 3DS Ocarina of Time released around the same time as Zelda: Skyward Sword, which explains the crossover references there. And likewise, they were removed from the new Ocarina of Time remake so as not to distract from everything else going on. "I do remember at the time the designers on the 3DS version were really interested in placing Easter Eggs like that throughout the game, and the timing of the release of Skyward Sword was such that it was perfect to go ahead and include that. So I said, 'Okay, sure,'" says Aonuma, but same as before with the Mario 64 references, "you don't want to interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game. So for that reason, we decided not to go that way." sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been a huge success for Nintendo, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game ever, shifting more than 5.2 million copies in four days. Nintendo announced the sales result this morning in a press release, specifying that the record relates only to Nintendo-published games. But since Nintendo's games are the most popular Switch 2 games, the fastest-selling-ever title presumably holds. It's an incredible result for a game that's been received with enormous enthusiasm. Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time five golden stars in Eurogamer's review , saying: "Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve." We've also already seen a jump in US Switch 2 sales because of the game's release. So much for not launching in November near GTA 6 , eh? This level of success begs the question of whether Nintendo would consider remaking more beloved old Zelda games - or Nintendo games - to replicate this nostalgia-driven effect. Are there other Zelda games that have the pull of Ocarina of Time that haven't been remade or remastered already in some capacity? sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Is Already the Second-Best-Selling Switch 2 Game
sources.text: The remake sold 5.2 million copies in 4 days, eclipsing Donkey Kong Bananza The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the fastest-selling Switch 2 game yet. On Wednesday, Nintendo announced that the remake of the 1998 classic sold more than 5.2 million copies worldwide in its first four days on sale — "the highest global sales for any Nintendo-published Nintendo Switch 2 game in its first four days." This also means that Ocarina of Time is likely already the second-best-selling Switch 2 game, period. Mario Kart World has sold over 16 million copies, but according to Nintendo's most recent financial figures , its second-best-selling title through the end of September was Donkey Kong Bananza , with 5.05 million copies sold. Nintendo only publishes sales figures for its own titles; it's possible that a third-party game has sold more than Ocarina and Bananza , although it's hard to imagine what that might be. Ocarina of Time is only Nintendo's second-biggest hit of 2026 so far, though. Tomodachi Life , for the original Switch, remains the champ for now with an amazing 8.8 million copies sold. Even so, Ocarina will likely eclipse it before the end of the year. After a somewhat controversial reveal, due to its radically different art style, Ocarina of Time has been met with widespread critical acclaim and looks like a strong awards contender , too.

sources.text: Weeks after the Switch 2 was jailbroken for the first time , Nintendo's latest system update has reportedly patched the exploit that could have allowed users to mod and dump games, putting a stop to those activities… at least for now. The initial jailbreak in question was always limited. Legitimate game-programming app SmileBASIC 4 – which could be downloaded straight from the Switch eShop prior to this whole debacle – could essentially serve as a gateway for exploits that could let folks access parts of the Switch 2 that the average user really isn't meant to reach. There was a catch, though – as a tethered jailbreak, it relied on the software and on it staying open – if you were to turn your system off, you'd have to repeat the entire jailbreak process when you turned it back on. Even so, hackers were still able to use this to dump Switch 2 games and their assets, as well as mod games like Mario Kart World – in fact, one of the jailbreak's first documented uses was putting Hatsune Miku, Peter Griffin, and Sanrio character Cinnamoroll into Nintendo's racing game. Now, though, according to modder and dataminer OatmealDome, that should no longer be the case thanks to Switch 2 system update 23.5.0, which rolled out a few hours ago. "The OS exploit used in the recent jailbreak has been patched in version 23.5.0," OatmealDome writes on Twitter. "Dumping and modding games will be impossible again from this point forward, with the exception of some cartridge games (and maybe game updates) that are released in the near future." They report that game exploits, like the aforementioned SmileBASIC 4 one as well as an exploit tied to physical copies of Civilization 7, still exist, but "it is no longer possible to 'escape' the game starting with 23.5.0. This effectively means that the capabilities of homebrew are locked to whatever the game can do already (i.e. not much)." There's no doubt that as far as Nintendo is concerned, this patch couldn't come soon enough. Mere hours after the release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, the game was running on PC after being dumped from a Switch 2 copy , which I can't imagine the house of Mario was particularly pleased about. Hardware nerds unite, sign up to our free tech newsletter for a weekly digest of the hottest new tech, the latest gadgets on the test bench, and much more from the team at GamesRadar+. But the question is, is Pandora's box now open? With exploits and the like, we often tend to see that striking down one thing just leads to another three appearing – just look at the literal thousands of clones of Switch emulator Yuzu that surfaced after Nintendo took down the original . Some have also claimed that this update may not be as effective as you might think. According to Twitter account SwitchTools , it'll still be possible to dump new physical games on this firmware – though Game Key Cards will be immune. "Digital games, updates, and DLC cannot be downloaded and dumped without [Nintendo Switch Online]," they say. Beyond that, multiple users online are expressing that they'll not be updating their system in order to keep access to the exploit, so it may not have been a perfect fix for Nintendo regardless. sources.text: The latest Zelda game is "off to a great start," says Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa Nintendo says The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is "off to a great start" and the 40th Anniversary Edition Switch 2 console has also been "very positive," heading off speculation from an investor that price hikes may be hurting momentum. Taking questions as part of its latest financial briefing , Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa is pressed on how well the Switch 2 is selling its wares after the console's price jumped to $500 earlier this year. Investors reckon things are slowing down, and they don't like that. As such, one asks the Nintendo suits whether they think current financial goals will still be met. The short answer is absolutely; just look at how well Zelda's Ocarina of Time remake and 40th-anniversary console are doing. "Adoption has progressed smoothly over the roughly one and a half years since Nintendo Switch 2 launched last June, and the installed base now exceeds 25 million units," Furukawa says. "At the end of last year's holiday season, we explained that there were regional differences in how well our expectations were met. But the March release of Pokemon Pokopia acted as a driver of global hardware sales, and we entered the new fiscal year with good momentum." Furukawa continues by saying that, while the Switch 2 did indeed increase in price, the impact hasn't been too great because most people were given plenty of notice and have had plenty of hardware and software bundles to compensate for it. That takes us to today, where Nintendo is seemingly riding high thanks to all things Zelda. Furukawa says the special version of the Switch 2 designed to celebrate Zelda's 40th anniversary has been "very positive" for the company and has "contributed to strong sales in various regions." Meanwhile, while it's too early to delve too far into the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake numbers, Furukawa says it's "off to a great start," and that Nintendo is in "good shape for the coming holiday season," too. "Holiday season sales significantly impact the number of units shipped annually for our dedicated video game platform business," he says. "Given the hardware price revisions, we think the sales trends over the next several weeks will be key to achieving our sales guidance." Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week While no official numbers are given, there are signs that, yeah, those Zelda products are shifting units. As per Circana, the Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 drove record sales for Nintendo in the US. In fact, it was only last month that a Nintendo exec said those at the house of Mario "underestimated" how well it would sell. Stock has been an issue, though a welcome one. We have less to go on with the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. That said, analyst firms say the N64 throwback is the largest physical launch in the UK so far this year. With the festive period coming up, I can see why Nintendo isn't sweating this one too hard right now. Nintendo "bearing" Switch 2 manufacturing costs to avoid price hikes – but that may have to change if "we cannot absorb the costs through our own efforts." sources.text: Nintendo Switch 2 The Legend of Zelda The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time What, Master Sword not good enough for you? You need a Biggoron Sword too? Well, okay, fine. In the Ocarina of Time remake, I guess I recommend it. The Biggoron Sword is an optional weapon obtained via a lengthy sidequest. It’s the strongest sword in the game, dealing even more damage than the Master Sword, but it’s slower, and requires two hands to wield, so no shield on the side. Still, having it around can be handy, so let’s go on a little adventure to get one. First, you need to be adult Link. It’s also helpful to have obtained the Bolero of Fire for one specific part, though it’s not mandatory. You will need to have unfrozen King Zora in Zora Domain, though, so you’ll have to have at minimum done the Ice Cavern and obtained blue fire to release him from the red ice. Oh, and you’ll also want to have Epona at the ready. The entire questline takes place in the adult era, so no need to swap back and forth between child and adult Link. As adult Link, start off in Kakariko Village by speaking to the Cucco Lady, who’s to your right when you enter town from Hyrule Field, minding her Cuccos. She’ll give you a Pocket Egg. Wait one day (or play Sun’s Song twice to speed things along) and it will hatch into a Pocket Cucco. Take that to the big house near the center of Kakariko Village where Talon is sleeping, and use the Pocket Cucco next to him to wake him up. Then, go back to the Cucco Lady and she’ll trade you the Pocket Cucco for the adorable blue Cojiro. Take Cojiro out to the Lost Woods. From the entrance head left to where Skull Kid used to hang out in child era, and you’ll find a man sleeping against a tree stump. Use Cojiro next to him to wake him up, and he’ll give you an Odd Mushroom, asking you to take it to an old lady back in Kakariko…in four minutes flat. Warning: Don’t do what I did and try to do this part of the quest right between Water Temple and Shadow Temple. The cutscene for Kakariko Village triggered as I entered, and in the time it took to play out, my timer for the quest ran out and I had to go back and get another mushroom from the guy. You can call Epona from the exit of Kokiri Forest and ride her fast to Kakariko and you’ll easily make it on time. Using a warp song like the Nocturne of Shadow will spoil your time, so don’t do it, though there’s no real reason to in this situation. The old lady is easily reached by entering the potion shop, exiting through the back door, and then walking through the backyard to the house next door. Show her the Odd Mushroom, and receive the Odd Poultice in return. You now have to return to the man in the Lost Woods, but there’s no time limit this time, so feel free to mosey at a leisurely pace. However, when you return to Kokiri Forest, the man isn’t there. Instead, Fado is waiting for you. She says some ominous stuff about humans turning into Stalfos, and gives you the Poacher’s Axe, with very little direction as to who it needs to go to. Fortunately, you have this guide! Your destination is just outside Gerudo Valley. You can cross the bridge freely if you’ve already finished the Spirit Temple, or you can use Epona to leap over the gap. The Master Craftsman is there, and he’ll take the saw from you and give you a Broken Goron Sword in return. Now we’re getting somewhere, I guess. Use the Bolero of Fire if you have it to get up to Death Mountain in a jiffy (don’t forget to equip your Goron Tunic), or just walk. You’re aiming for the summit, where Biggoron is hanging out, hammering away. Give him the Broken Goron Sword to fix, but he can’t do it without eyedrops. He hands you a prescription, which you’ll need to take to King Zora back in Zora Domain. Whew. Almost done. King Zora will give you the Eyeball Frog, which needs to go back to the scientist in the hut at Lake Hylia in just two and a half minutes. If you’ve already thawed out Zora’s Domain, this is a quick trip through the underwater tunnel. Otherwise, you’d better sprint: you can’t use Serenade of Water, or the frog will spoil. The Lake Scientist can make your medicine, but it once again comes with a timer, and this one’s a doozy. You need to get all the way from Lake Hylia to the summit of Death Mountain, and you can’t warp. Using the Bolero of Fire (or any other warp) will cut the time on your medicine down to just ten seconds, and there’s no way to get from the center of Death Mountain Crater outside to Biggoron in that short a time. Head outside the scientist’s house instead, and call Epona. Ride like the wind across Hyrule Field, through Kakariko, and up Death Mountain, dodging boulders as you go. You have a little bit of wiggle room on the timer if you get hit by rocks a few times, but don’t dilly dally. Biggoron is thrilled, and gets to work on your sword. It’s going to take three days to make, so he gives you a receipt to hang onto for the pickup. You can either go do other stuff for three in-game days, or play the Sun’s Song six times to speed things along. At the end of it, show him the receipt, and the Biggoron Sword is yours at last. I just want to play with my silly little toys and solve my silly little puzzles without fighting the elements to survive It's such a night and day difference, you'll be hearing A-R-X-A-R-X in your head the first time you try it out. sources.text: It’s outsold titles like A Link Between Worlds and Echoes of Wisdom in less than a week Nintendo has announced that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake sold 5.2 million units in its first four days. Nintendo’s total includes both physical and digital sales â reports from other tracking and charting companies will report lower sales numbers, because Nintendo doesn’t provide digital sales data, meaning they tend to only report on physical sales. While it’s likely it’s also the fastest-selling Switch 2 game overall, Nintendo can only claim it’s the fastest-selling first-party title because not all third-party publishers â especially those who release multi-format titles â share sales figures per console. Na indústria de games, isso significa que a versão final destinada à distribuição foi oficialmente concluída e a etapa principal de desenvolvimento chegou ao fim. Normalmente, o anúncio de que um jogo atingiu esse estágio acontece semanas antes do lançamento, já que as empresas precisam preparar cópias físicas, embalagens e a distribuição para lojas — mesmo que o conteúdo da mídia física seja apenas um código digital. “Neste momento, a Rockstar concluiu o desenvolvimento de GTA 6”, confirmou Zelnick na teleconferência de resultados da última segunda (09), reiterando que a Rockstar fez “o seu melhor trabalho até agora”. Como a distribuição digital não depende do envio de discos para fábricas, a Rockstar pode concentrar os preparativos na versão digital e na infraestrutura da PlayStation Network. Informações sobre os arquivos hospedados na rede da Sony também indicam que a estrutura de distribuição do jogo já está preparada. O status Gold, no entanto, não significa que todo o trabalho terminou. A equipe ainda pode desenvolver uma atualização de primeiro dia, realizar testes nos servidores e corrigir possíveis problemas antes da estreia. Com o lançamento marcado para 19 de novembro, os números ainda podem crescer nos próximos dias. Desse total, 7,23 milhões correspondem à versão de PlayStation 5, enquanto 2,46 milhões são referentes aos consoles Xbox Series X|S. A diferença também aparece na receita estimada. As vendas no PlayStation representam aproximadamente US$ 703 milhões, contra US$ 239 milhões no Xbox. A divisão acompanha a maior presença do PS5 no mercado de consoles, além dos direitos de marketing de GTA 6 associados à Sony. sources.title: 'I think we'd accidentally created the most hardcore extraction game of all time:' EVE Vanguard is taking hard-won playtest lessons into a '24/7 Alpha'
sources.text: It's not early access, not yet. Super-early access. Tomorrow, November 10, EVE Online is releasing a new expansion, Fractured Skies , and companion FPS EVE Vanguard is going into something Fenris Creations is calling a 24/7 alpha. Formal early access on Steam is coming late next year, but you can buy the game and play it through EVE's own client⁠ —and it won't go away like prior playtests. Tomorrow will also see Vanguard start to fulfill its promise as a linked game to EVE Online⁠—completing contracts in the multiplayer FPS will create military campaign opportunities players can find and act on in EVE—marking the return of a dream Fenris (formerly CCP Games) has pursued since the ill-fated PS3 shooter, Dust 514 . I sat down with Vanguard game director Scott Davis and EVE design director Greg Hennessey to talk about what's coming tomorrow and further down the line. From a pure gameplay perspective, Davis told me that NPC AI and new player onboarding are the biggest improvements in Vanguard since its last playtest . The NPC enemies inhabiting Vanguard's levels just weren't challenging enough, and while it's easy to make them better shots, the problem was more one of tactical depth. "We had a lot of people bounce off the game pretty hard in July," Davis said of the other issue, Vanguard's new player experience. "I think we'd accidentally created the most hardcore extraction game of all time, because we had some awkward intricacies to how weapon upgrading and healing worked in the game." There will be more direct tutorializing to address this in tomorrow's Alpha, and a lot of thought has also gone into how Vanguard introduces its modes to players. New players will be introduced through a full co-op/PvE mode, which will then unlock the PvEvP from the last playtest. The final mode sounds the most exciting and unique, though: Davis described it as a PvP-first "3v3v3 procedurally generated labyrinth, where you just go in and only one team can get out alive." That sounds sick, and reminds me a bit of Marathon's Cryo Archive pinnacle activity. I'm encouraged by the variety of playstyle options Vanguard is offering: Marathon seems to have ultimately been sunk by its pure focus on hardcore PvP, while Vanguard might have an advantage attracting and holding a healthy playerbase with such varied modes. The back of the box pitch for Vanguard is that what happens in the FPS will impact EVE Online's one-of-a-kind digital economy, and vice versa. I keep saying it's like the jocks (FPS guys) teaming up with the nerds ( spreadsheet EVE guys), and people generally smile politely when I do. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. The 24/7 alpha is coming with a first version of that interoperability, with mission completion unlocking mining and combat activities in EVE Online. The next big step in this connection is planned for the second quarter of 2027. At that point, Fenris plans for Vanguard players to be able to declare allegiance with one of the four main empires in EVE, then have their mission progress contribute to the Military Campaign and Conquest systems introduced in EVE's latest two expansions. Davis sees the empire allegiance system as a major step by Vanguard toward EVE's style of emergent player behavior. One thing he's looking forward to: Vanguard players adopting faction heraldry on their characters, and the sorts of Arc Raiders moments it may foment out in the wild. Maybe you hold fire on a stranger in PvEvP mode because you recognize you're both aligned with the same faction. Alternately, maybe you go out of your way to hunt down a player because they're aligned with an opposing empire. I was curious if linking the two games had presented any technical difficulties, but both Davis and Hennessey told me it's been surprisingly smooth sailing. "We've sent up many flares ourselves before, but we haven't really had many messages back," Davis told me. "And I wouldn't call it a technical hurdle, because everyone's been working really hard and they know how to do it. But I think that there will be a champagne popping moment of getting those first messages back from EVE Online." Hennessey, meanwhile, said it's less an issue of connecting the two games. Rather, he pointed out that making a game is hard, making two is twice as hard, and that these two games of very different genres have to align with and compliment each other. But I hope it pays off, because this vision of two, nested live games changing and influencing each other in real time is like nothing else out there. sources.text: Soul Reaver 2 e Freedom Wars Remastered entram no PlayStation Plus Deluxe. Neste mês, embarque em uma missão inspiradora de conexão humana em Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, reúna uma tripulação única enquanto navega o alto-mar em Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii, explore ruínas controladas por seitas, cavernas naturais e bunkers nucleares de uma zona rural britânica inóspita e coberta de vegetação em Atomfall, ou explore um vasto mapa repleto de locais cativantes em Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake. Todos esses títulos e muitos outros estão disponíveis na seleção de novembro do Catálogo de jogos do PlayStation Plus *. Enquanto isso, Soul Reaver 2 e Freedom Wars Remastered chegam ao PlayStation Plus Deluxe. Embarque em uma missão inspiradora de conexão humana que vai além da UCA. Acompanhe Sam no próximo capítulo de sua jornada, enquanto ele tenta conectar a Austrália à Rede Quiral. Explore um ambiente natural passando por ciclos diurnos e noturnos, além de desastres naturais, incluindo terremotos, tempestades de areia e incêndios florestais, e a Chuva temporal, uma chuva que envelhece instantaneamente tudo o que toca. Para atravessar esta paisagem perigosa, você precisará construir novos tipos de infraestrutura, dominar equipamentos especializados e enfrentar (ou evitar) as criaturas sobrenaturais que vagam pelo mundo fragmentado. Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii | PS5, PS4 Uma nova lenda começa quando você assume o papel de Goro Majima, um homem que perdeu a memória e se reinventa como um pirata em alto-mar. Embarque em uma aventura pirata intensa e moderna com um ex-yakuza que virou capitão pirata e sua tripulação, enquanto eles travam combates eletrizantes em terra e no mar em busca de memórias perdidas e de um tesouro lendário. Atomfall, um jogo de ação e sobrevivência inspirado em fatos reais, se passa cinco anos após o acidente nuclear de Windscale, no norte da Inglaterra. Explore a área de quarentena fictícia, procure suprimentos, crie itens, negocie, lute e use a lábia para sobreviver em um cenário no interior da Inglaterra repleto de personagens bizarros, misticismo, seitas e agências governamentais clandestinas. Produzido por Rebellion, o estúdio por trás de Sniper Elite e Zombie Army, Atomfall desafiará você a desvendar o sombrio mistério do que realmente aconteceu. Uma releitura impressionante da aclamada obra-prima de RPG e o início narrativo da Trilogia Erdrick. Há muitos anos, o grande herói Ortega despediu-se da esposa e do filho ao partir em uma jornada para derrotar o vilão Baramos, o arquidemônio. Ortega falhou em sua missão, e Baramos ainda ameaça o mundo. Agora, ao completar 16 anos, o único filho de Ortega é convocado pelo rei de Aliahan e recebe uma missão da mais alta importância: assumir a jornada de Ortega, derrotar Baramos e salvar o mundo. Em Trepang2, você assume o papel de um soldado fugitivo que não tem lembranças de sua vida anterior, mas possui habilidades sobrenaturais. A vingança não sai da sua cabeça, e você não medirá esforços para conseguir o que quer. Desfira golpes devastadores, esconda-se nas sombras, empunhe armas explosivas e faça os vilões provarem do próprio veneno. Revide, descubra a verdade e enfrente uma ameaça ainda mais mortal do que você. Vivencie toda a intensidade do Campeonato de MotoGP de 2026 com todos os pilotos, equipes, motos e circuitos oficiais de forma mais autêntica: pela primeira vez, os resultados do mundo real atualizam dinamicamente as classificações dos pilotos, influenciando diretamente o desempenho no jogo ao longo da temporada. Destaque-se e acompanhe sua jornada com cartões colecionáveis deslumbrantes que celebram seu progresso. Junte-se à experiência em constante expansão de Hell Let Loose: um jogo de tiro em primeira pessoa hardcore ambientado na Segunda Guerra Mundial, com batalhas épicas de 100 jogadores que envolvem infantaria, tanques, artilharia, uma linha de frente em constante mudança e um metajogo original baseado em recursos, inspirado em jogos de estratégia em tempo real (RTS). Entre na batalha em partidas de vários jogadores de 50 vs. 50 em mapas enormes. Escolha uma das 14 missões na infantaria, os tipos de unidades de reconhecimento e armadura, cada uma equipada com armas, veículos e equipamentos diferentes. Jogue como oficial, batedor, artilheiro, médico, engenheiro, comandante de tanque e muito mais para vivenciar todos os aspectos dos combates da Segunda Guerra Mundial. Cricket 26 – The Official Game of the Ashes | PS5, PS4 Com a novíssima carreira de gestão, uma equipe profissional maior e melhor, o modo Ashes mais completo e um maior controle dentro e fora de campo, graças à gameplay aprimorada e às estratégias detalhadas, o Cricket 26 apresenta u confronto épico. Soul Reaver 2 | PS5, PS4 Nesta sequência do aclamado Legacy of Kain: Soul Reaver, assuma novamente o papel de Raziel e lute para voltar, atravessando as areias do tempo, às épocas decisivas e perigosas do passado de Nosgoth em sua busca implacável por Kain. Enfrente novos inimigos enquanto desvenda os mistérios das antigas civilizações de Nosgoth e revele os planos que estão por trás da corrupção dos Pilares. Em um futuro distante, onde todos os recursos da Terra se esgotaram, estar vivo já é um pecado por si só. Condenado a uma pena de prisão de um milhão de anos, você precisa sobreviver a missões letais para ter qualquer esperança de liberdade. Morra na prisão ou viva no combate. A escolha é sua. Use Thorn, sua arma mais confiável, para dominar o campo de batalha. Lute ao lado de aliados e do Acessório, seu ciborgue guardião, para enfrentar inimigos poderosos. *O Catálogo de Jogos PlayStation Plus e os títulos para PlayStation Plus Deluxe podem variar de acordo com a região. sources.title: Side Effects Guaranteed in the First DLC For The Outer Worlds 2, Coming December 2
sources.text: A distress signal beckons you and your crew of the Incognito to a derelict ship, where you discover the ship’s crew in suspended animation. All signs point to foul play, especially the puddle of what was most likely a person. You recover a video message left by the captain of the vessel, who explains that the crew has been contaminated with something while on a heist that will cause explosive cell death unless they find a cure. And by explosive cell death, she means more like a… “liquefaction”. By the looks of the puddle on the floor: liquefaction indeed. The stakes are set for the release of the first of a two-part narrative DLC expansion of The Outer Worlds 2 on December 2. In Side Effects Guaranteed , the video message you found leads you to Gordon Hazen, one of the leading agents in Sub Rosa, a criminal organization made up of like-minded individuals who have chosen to live their lives stealing from the various factions instead of working for them. Gordon in turn sends you to Elysium Valley, a new region on Eden that is home to a settlement of former Protectorate subjects that have been forgotten by their Protectorate leaders. He believes they may have the answers to saving his crew. He personally favors diplomacy over violence but needs you to do whatever you need to in order to get the information he needs. But Gordon isn’t the only one with interest in Elysium Valley. Another Sub Rosa agent, Algernon Lankester, wants to recruit you to help him exploit the subjects for his own personal gain. The fate of the subjects, the frozen Sub Rosa agents, and the future of Sub Rosa itself is up for you, our intrepid Commander, to decide. A new narrative story is not all that will be coming when Side Effects Guaranteed launches in a few weeks, however. Along with the new region of Elysium Valley to explore, players will encounter new threats like vicious canids and primal sprats. What’s a primal sprat? Just a normal sprat, but about 100 times the size. Surely, they’re just as friendly and forgiving of all the time you “accidentally” shot their much smaller cousins while exploring Arcadia. With these new threats comes the ability to make your Commander even stronger and, of course, more flawed (but in a good way). The level cap will increase from 30 to 36, bringing more skill points to broaden your build. Being able to go to level 36 also means there are three more perks you can acquire, with 15 brand new perks being added into the mix. Four new flaws will also be introduced that can change how your Commander plays, like “Lethally Tolerant,” a flaw that recognizes your built-up resistance to chemicals so your max toxicity will increase. This is great in the moment, but if you ever experience a Toxicity Crash, you will die instantly. Another example is “Must Have Been the Wind,” which will mark an “assassination target” for a combat group. Killing the target will grant a 20% damage and speed buff until the combat ends, but failing to do so or attacking someone who isn’t the target applies a 10% damage and speed debuff to the player for 30 seconds. Truly rewards that come with great risks. Side Effects Guaranteed will also see new weapons, new armors, and new outfits for each of the companions, as well as a brand-new Sub Rosa-run radio station featuring 20 new songs for the game. For those who want to jump straight to the action in the DLC, a new alternate starting point is being added to the main menu when you choose a new game that will allow you to start with a custom save that lands you at the start of the DLC. Start the game, allot your skill and perk points, and enjoy Side Effects Guaranteed right away! This jam-packed adventure with a deep story and systems to build your ideal commander will set up the next DLC for The Outer Worlds 2 that will be coming in Spring of 2027, and choices made will directly impact the next DLC. Part one of this overarching expansion story, Side Effects Guaranteed , will release on December 2 for $14.99, or is available in the Premium Edition or Premium Edition Upgrade for The Outer Worlds 2 .

sources.text: Despite Obsidian layoffs, The Outer Worlds 2 is getting two expansions A story expansion for The Outer Worlds 2 has been announced, coming December 2. sources.text: Owlcat Games has revealed a release date for its tactical role-playing sequel Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy. The game arrives 28th January, 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X. A Switch 2 release date will be provided "at a later date", a press release says. Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy follows the good work laid down by Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader a couple of years ago. "Rogue Trader nails the 40k setting and provides an appropriately massive narrative filled with meaty tactical combat, though some bugs and poor performance hold it back," wrote Caeyln Ellis in Eurogamer's Warhammer 40,000 Rogue Trade review . Dark Heresy changes things by casting you as an Inquisitor and tasking you with hunting down heretics and purging the world of dark influences, as one is wont to do in the 41st century, it seems. And developer Owlcat has apparently overhauled many of the systems underpinning the adventure. There's a beta that's been running for a while that offers a complete first Act to try, and it's accessible if you buy a Founders edition of the game. This beta, incidentally, disappears 7th January, when Owlcat prepares the game for launch. Meanwhile, Owlcat is making a substantially different RPG based around the popular Expanse license - a game that's much more closely inspired by Mass Effect . That project recently recruited the help of former Dragon Age writer David Gaider , and it will no doubt hope to fill a much-lamented hole created recently by the cancellation of Mass Effect 5 .
